items.claim: Two snapToContainer behaviors on one binding share one dwell state
items.note: plus baedc6278b, which keeps the new armed-swap state through `createPart` so the gate's part-cache check passes.

items.claim: A root leaving a layout container moves its envelope members in the old frame
A scrolled source container gets unscrolled bounds in the preview and scrolled bounds on release
items.note: One `contentBoxOf` helper now gives the box to the source reflow, the release, and the drop candidate.

items.claim: swapOnDrop swaps the selected node instead of the node the drag moves
The descendant carry, reflow carry, and source reflow's "did it move" test measure with the bare projection instead of each node's own descriptor
items.note: The same mistake was in `selectionCenter`, `catchGliding`, and `capturePlaneRefs`, fixed in the same commit.

items.claim: A layer with a singular plane throws at press
items.note: with a correction. The throw is real, but it comes from an identity plane map: `invertPlane` answers null for the identity, and the code asserted non-null. A zero-scale plane doesn't throw; its non-finite move is already skipped, and a regression test covers it.

items.claim: A layout drop pulls a selected child out of its selected parent
items.note: The same gap was in `snapToContainer`'s plant, the layout release's sources and exits, `rootTranslateOps`, and the pageDrop loop. All of them now use the session's outermost dragged ids.

items.claim: An armed swap previews the layout insertion, but the release commits the swap
items.note: The drop previews stand down while a swap is armed. The documented rule that a later behavior's pose wins was left alone.

items.claim: `moveLead` is cached by delta alone, so a landing that changes at the same delta is ignored
